hero.name: Yanrui Chen
hero.role: MSc in Artificial Intelligence · Real-time ML for wearable robotics
hero.summary: I am a Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence candidate at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, working at the point where machine learning has to run on real hardware in real time. My current work at Shenzhen Yunmostar builds EMG-and-IMU driven gait control for industrial exoskeletons, where a model is only useful if it clears its latency budget. Before that I trained on computer engineering at CUHK-Shenzhen, and I have since shipped projects spanning medical ultrasound segmentation, LLM fine-tuning, and a high-concurrency live auction backend.
highlights: Built the industry's first EMG-fused real-time gait start/stop detection system for an exoskeleton
Fine-tuned a 90M-parameter ViT encoder to lift ultrasound lesion IoU from 0.093 to 0.737
Designed a fully asynchronous Redis bidding pipeline holding 11.4 ms average latency under load
Comfortable across the stack: model training, embedded signal processing, and the services around them

paragraphs: I build systems where a model has to survive contact with the physical world. At Yunmostar I designed, from scratch, a real-time gait start/stop detection system that fuses 10 channels of EMG with 78 channels of inertial signals to drive an industrial exoskeleton. The hard part was never the architecture — it was holding a precision target above 85% while staying inside a real-time control loop, which is why the final design pairs a dual-scale causal TCN with multi-seed ensembling and a gated confirmation stage to suppress false triggers.

That same instinct for the constraint, rather than the benchmark, runs through the rest of my work. I replaced a lab-bound force plate with a smart-insole calibration method that combines static double-support constraints with CNN-BiLSTM vertical ground reaction force prediction, reaching 0.15 body-weight cross-subject accuracy. I fine-tuned MedSAM's image encoder on ultrasound data to remove its dependence on manual prompts, and I built a data cleaning pipeline that turned a noisy corpus into something a lightweight LLM could actually learn from.

I am currently finishing my MSc in Artificial Intelligence at CUHK, after a BEng in Computer Engineering at CUHK-Shenzhen. Outside of coursework I like problems with a hard number attached to them — a latency budget, an accuracy floor, a crash-recovery deadline.

experience.organization: Shenzhen Yunmostar Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd.
experience.summary: Building the sensing and control algorithms that let an industrial exoskeleton read human intent and estimate human pose in real time.
highlights: Exoskeleton start/stop control had no industrial precedent using EMG, so the system had to be built from scratch against a Precision ≥ 85% target; I designed a real-time detection system fusing 10 channels of EMG with 78 channels of inertial signals, using a dual-scale causal TCN with gated confirmation to suppress false triggers.
The system reached 88.2% initiation Recall and 86.2% termination Precision, meeting the requirements for real-time control deployment.

Exoskeleton control requires accurate human pose input; I reproduced the GlobalPose method and adapted it to the production pipeline, optimizing along both matrix calibration and model training, with mocap ground truth guiding recalibration of the forearm RSB transform matrix.
Reduced local rotation error by 17.0% (19.63° → 16.29°) and left-wrist relative error by 76.9%, substantially improving upper-body pose accuracy.

Raw insole signals cannot directly represent vertical ground reaction force, and professional force measurement equipment is expensive and hard to scale; I proposed a force-plate-free insole vertical force calibration method combining static double-support constraints with CNN-BiLSTM dynamic force prediction, reaching 0.15 body-weight cross-subject accuracy.

experience.organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
experience.role: Research — Predicting Ultrafast Nonlinear Dynamics in Fibre Optics with LSTM
experience.summary: Predicting ultrafast nonlinear dynamics in optical fibres is computationally expensive, and conventional numerical methods struggle with the complex-valued nature of the data.
highlights: Engineered a customized LSTM cell in Python designed to process complex-valued data, and trained the network on optical pulse propagation data under Prof. Yuan Luo.
Validated that recurrent neural networks can effectively forecast propagation pulses in optical fibres, demonstrating their capacity to handle complex data in nonlinear dynamic environments.

projects.title: Full-stack Live-stream E-commerce Auction System
projects.tagline: Millisecond bid synchronization without synchronous database writes.
highlights: Designed a fully asynchronous bidding pipeline using pure in-memory Redis operations with 5-second batch persistence to MySQL.
Implemented Lua-script atomic distributed locks, Redis ZSet real-time leaderboards, per-user rate limiting, and a triple-heartbeat self-healing daemon.
Built a React and TypeScript frontend with a Node.js and Socket.IO backend and one-click Docker deployment.
Sustained 1,000+ concurrent users per live room at a 98.4% bid success rate with 11.4 ms average and 65 ms P99 latency.
Recovered all active auctions within 1 second after a full Redis crash, with zero manual intervention.

projects.title: VLM-based Medical Ultrasound Anomaly Detection
projects.tagline: Removing MedSAM's dependence on manual position prompts.
highlights: Benchmarked raw MedSAM to quantify its prompt-free limitations in automated clinical workflows.
Froze the prompt encoder and fine-tuned the 90M-parameter ViT image encoder and mask decoder on the BUS-UCLM and BUSI ultrasound datasets with a hybrid BCE and Dice loss.
Used patient-level data splits to prevent leakage between training and evaluation.
Improved IoU from 0.093 to 0.737 and F1 from 0.157 to 0.823 on BUS-UCLM.
Generalized to the unseen BUSI dataset, sustaining 12 FPS inference on a single RTX 4090.

projects.title: Data Cleaning and Fine-tuning for a Lightweight LLM
projects.tagline: Turning a noisy corpus into something a small model can actually learn from.
highlights: Diagnosed formatting issues, quality problems and semantic inconsistencies in the raw dataset, which made it unsuitable for effective fine-tuning.
Designed a data cleaning pipeline addressing non-standard roles, missing fields, duplicate text and semantic consistency, then ran full fine-tuning with optimized hyperparameters in LLaMA-Factory.
The cleaned dataset markedly improved model performance while holding base model capability on other benchmarks.

projects.title: Personalized Email Agent for a Campus Context
projects.tagline: On-device email triage that avoids cloud privacy risk and API cost.
highlights: Designed a multi-agent system on the ERNIE-Speed (10–15B) model using a parallel-serial pipeline.
Implemented Chain-of-Thought prompting and retrieval-augmented generation over a campus knowledge base.
Reached near-human labelling accuracy with precise extraction of course names, professors and deadlines, eliminating API costs and keeping deployment privacy-preserving and on-device.

projects.title: Brick Building Game with Leap Motion in Unity
projects.tagline: Gesture-driven construction in a hand-tracked 3D space.
highlights: Developed a Unity-based brick building game integrating Leap Motion hand tracking.
Implemented gesture recognition for brick selection, rotation and placement using C# scripting.
Delivered a functional prototype that lets players build brick structures using hand gestures.

projects.title: Smoothing and Edge Enhancement for Artistic Style Images
projects.tagline: Classical image processing to restyle a photograph.
highlights: Combined smoothing and edge detection to transform an image into a different artistic style through edge enhancement.
Designed colour adjustment and image merge methods to optimize the visual result.
Implemented the functions in Python and MATLAB and achieved acceptable results.

projects.title: Content-Based Image Retrieval with a Database System
projects.tagline: Pairing feature matching with a relational store.
highlights: Worked as a team member to combine image retrieval with a database system.
Designed the database schema for image storage, feature storage and picture matching.
Integrated Python and MySQL code to achieve picture access and feature access.

projects.title: 2-Player Bouncing Ball Game on a Cortex-M3 Board
projects.tagline: A real-time game on bare-metal embedded hardware.
highlights: Wrote C++ code to implement and synchronize GPIO, USART, LCD, external interrupts and timers on a Cortex-M3 development board.
Delivered a smooth, lag-free gaming experience on embedded hardware, demonstrating low-level programming and embedded systems expertise.
